title: Relational Data
description: Can model a domain as constrained tables, write SQL that joins and aggregates at the right grain, and choose an index from a measured plan rather than a rule of thumb.

levels.name: Foundation
levels.description: Can draw an ER diagram that matches a CREATE TABLE script, name the primary and foreign keys, and write a SELECT with a join — under written guidance.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Can design a small PostgreSQL schema whose constraints reject a deliberate invalid insert, write queries with joins, aggregation and a CTE or subquery, and explain a normalization decision against that schema.

levels.name: Practitioner
levels.description: Can independently ship ordered migrations from an empty database, load sample data, interpret EXPLAIN ANALYZE for a query the API actually runs, and keep or reject an index from recorded times rather than blanket rules.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Can diagnose a constraint or query failure where the diagram looked correct, show the rejected write or the misleading plan, and defend a denormalization or isolation choice with a measured trade-off.

levels.name: Mastery Evidence
levels.description: Can review another apprentice's schema, name a missing constraint or a vanity index, and teach when a join-heavy relational model is the wrong store on an unfamiliar domain.
